in_arabic.name: مجاهد
in_arabic.meaning: المجاهد في سبيل الله، مقاتل ضد الظالمين
in_arabic.long_meaning: المجاهد هو من يجاهد في سبيل الله تعالى، ويقاتل ضد الظالمين والكافرين، وهو الشخص الذي يبذل قصارى جهده في الجهاد في سبيل الله، سواء كان الجهاد باليد أو باللسان أو بالقلب. وردت كلمة المجاهد في القرآن الكريم في سورة النساء آية 95: «لَا يَقْفُلُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَلَا الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ إِذَا قُضِيَ لَهُمُ الْأَمْرُ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِن يَكُن لَّهُمُ الْحَقُّ يُخَلِفُونَ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَلَكِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَخْلِفُونَ أَمْرَهُ إِذَا كُتِبَ أَمْرُهُ أَوَلًا أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُخَلِفُونَ وَلَيْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ حَرَجٌ فِي مَا أَطَعْنَ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِن كَانَ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ خِلْفَةً ظَاهِرَةً»

in_urdu.name: مجاہد
in_urdu.meaning: اللہ کی راہ میں جدوجہد کرنے والا، ظالموں کے خلاف لڑنے والا
in_urdu.long_meaning: مجاہد وہ شخص ہے جو اللہ کی راہ میں جدوجہد کرتا ہے اور ظالموں اور کافروں کے خلاف لڑتا ہے۔ یہ شخص اپنی طاقت اور وسائل کے مطابق اللہ کی راہ میں جدوجہد کرتا ہے، چاہے وہ ہتھیاروں کے ذریعے ہو یا اپنے الفاظ اور دل کے ذریعے۔ قرآن مجید میں مجاہد کا ذکر نساء سورة آیت 95 میں کیا گیا ہے: «لَا يَقْفُلُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَلَا الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ إِذَا قُضِيَ لَهُمُ الْأَمْرُ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِن يَكُن لَّهُمُ الْحَقُّ يُخَلِفُونَ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَلَكِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَخْلِفُونَ أَمْرَهُ إِذَا كُتِبَ أَمْرُهُ أَوَلًا أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُخَلِفُونَ وَلَيْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ حَرَجٌ فِي مَا أَطَعْنَ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِن كَانَ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ خِلْفَةً ظَاهِرَةً»

in_hindi.name: मुजाहिद
in_hindi.meaning: अल्लाह की राह में संघर्ष करने वाला, जालिमों के खिलाफ लड़ने वाला
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुजाहिद वह व्यक्ति है जो अल्लाह की राह में संघर्ष करता है और जालिमों और काफिरों के खिलाफ लड़ता है। यह व्यक्ति अपनी शक्ति और संसाधनों के अनुसार अल्लाह की राह में संघर्ष करता है, चाहे वह हथियारों के माध्यम से हो या अपने शब्दों और दिल के माध्यम से। कुरआन मजीद में मुजाहिद का उल्लेख सूरा نساء आयत 95 में किया गया है: «لَا يَقْفُلُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَلَا الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ إِذَا قُضِيَ لَهُمُ الْأَمْرُ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِن يَكُن لَّهُمُ الْحَقُّ يُخَلِفُونَ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَلَكِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَخْلِفُونَ أَمْرَهُ إِذَا كُتِبَ أَمْرُهُ أَوَلًا أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُخَلِفُونَ وَلَيْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ حَرَجٌ فِي مَا أَطَعْنَ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِن كَانَ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ خِلْفَةً ظَاهِرَةً»

in_pashto.name: مجاهد
in_pashto.meaning: د الله په لاره کې د جهاد کوونکی، ظالمانو خلاف د جګړې کوونکی
in_pashto.long_meaning: مجاهد هغه څوک دی چې د الله په لاره کې جهاد کوي او ظالمانو او کافرو سره جګړه کوي. دا سړی د خپل توان او سرچینو سره سم د الله په لاره کې جهاد کوي، که د لاس په وسیله یا د خولې او زړه په وسیله. قرآن کریم کې د مجاهد کلمه د نساء سورې په 95 آیت کې راغلې ده: «لَا يَقْفُلُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَلَا الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ إِذَا قُضِيَ لَهُمُ الْأَمْرُ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِن يَكُن لَّهُمُ الْحَقُّ يُخَلِفُونَ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَلَكِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَخْلِفُونَ أَمْرَهُ إِذَا كُتِبَ أَمْرُهُ أَوَلًا أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُخَلِفُونَ وَلَيْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ حَرَجٌ فِي مَا أَطَعْنَ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِن كَانَ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ خِلْفَةً ظَاهِرَةً»

in_english.name: Mujaahid
in_english.meaning: One who strives in the cause of Allah, fighter against oppressors
in_english.long_meaning: Mujaahid (المجاهد) is a term used in Islam to describe a person who strives in the cause of Allah (God). The term is derived from the Arabic root 'J-H-D' (ج-ه-د), which means 'to strive' or 'to struggle'. A Mujaahid is someone who engages in jihad, which can take various forms including armed struggle against oppressors and non-believers, as well as internal spiritual struggle. The concept of Mujaahid is rooted in the Quran and Hadith, and has been a significant part of Islamic tradition and history. In the Quran, the term is mentioned in Surah An-Nisa, verse 95: «لَا يَقْفُلُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ وَلَا الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ إِذَا قُضِيَ لَهُمُ الْأَمْرُ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِن يَكُن لَّهُمُ الْحَقُّ يُخَلِفُونَ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَلَكِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَخْلِفُونَ أَمْرَهُ إِذَا كُتِبَ أَمْرُهُ أَوَلًا أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ الْمُخَلِفُونَ وَلَيْسَ عَلَى الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ حَرَجٌ فِي مَا أَطَعْنَ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ وَإِن كَانَ مِنَ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِ خِلْفَةً ظَاهِرَةً»

data.cultural_impact: The name Mujaahid holds significant cultural importance as it relates to the concept of Jihad, a central tenet in Islamic tradition. This term embodies the idea of self-sacrifice and dedication to a righteous cause. Mujaahids are often considered heroic figures who have given their all for their beliefs, and have left an indelible mark on history. Their struggles, whether physical or spiritual, serve to illustrate the resilience and determination of the Muslim community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Mujaahid represents the ongoing struggle to align one's actions with the divine will of Allah. It is a reminder of the importance of striving for own betterment and seeking closeness to the Creator. This can take many forms, such as engaging in acts of worship, morally upright living, or even personal introspection. Ultimately, the name encapsulates the idea that a true believer is one who never stops striving towards a better self and a closer relationship with the Divine.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: The term 'Mujaahid' was initially used to describe the Arab fighters who participated in the early Islamic conquests (632-750 CE) to defend and expand the Muslim territories against the Byzantine and Sassanian empires. They were considered the pioneers of jihad (holy war) and were granted tax exemptions and other privileges for their sacrifices.
historical_references.context: Defence and expansion of Muslim territories against the Byzantine and Sassanian empires

historical_references.reference: During the 8th and 9th centuries CE, the term 'Mujaahid' was also used to refer to the Muslim scholars and students of Islamic sciences who traveled from their homes to study in the major Islamic centers, such as Baghdad and Damascus. They were often supported financially by the Islamic state and were considered to be engaged in a spiritual jihad, or struggle, for the advancement of Islamic knowledge.
historical_references.context: Spiritual jihad for the advancement of Islamic knowledge

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Mujaahid' originally referred to an Islamic warrior or fighter for a just cause, but in modern contexts, it has been associated with Islamist extremist groups involved in global jihad and terrorism. On social media platforms, Mujaahid is used to refer to individuals who engage in online propaganda and recruitment for such groups. In news media, Mujaahid is frequently used to describe members of organizations like al-Qaeda, ISIS, and Boko Haram. In the realm of cybercrime, Mujaahid cyber cells are groups of hackers who use their skills to support Islamist extremist causes, often launching cyberattacks against government and civilian targets.
